title: The 10 Best Utility Knives
subtitle: Retractable, folding and flip-open utility knives and box cutters, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A utility knife takes cheap replaceable blades for cutting boxes, carpet, drywall and rope. We ranked 10 best-sellers from WORKPRO, Klein, Milwaukee, STANLEY, REXBETI and others on rating, review volume and features (quick blade changes, blade storage, spare blades and a metal body). They're inexpensive enough that many people keep one in every drawer and toolbox.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

avoid.name: Milwaukee FASTBACK Folding Utility Knife w/Blade Multifunctionality, Red-black
avoid.flag: Sold as a utility knife; bullets describe a pocket knife
avoid.verdict: The title says utility knife, but the listing describes a folding pocket knife with a fixed tanto blade and screwdriver bits, not one that takes replaceable utility blades.
reasons: The bullets describe a 'Stainless Steel Blade, partially Serrated' and a 'Stays Sharp Tanto Blade': a fixed pocket-knife blade, not the snap-in utility blades shoppers searching for a utility knife expect.
Nothing in the listing mentions blade changes or spare blades, so when it dulls you sharpen it rather than swap a blade.
If you want a Milwaukee utility knife, the Fastback 48-22-1502 has tool-free blade changes and blade storage for less.

buyers_guide.a: Retractable knives slide the blade back into the handle and are safest in a toolbox. Folding knives close like a pocket knife and ride on a belt clip. Flip-open knives like Milwaukee's Fastback and DEWALT's push-and-flip open with one hand.
Nearly all of these take the standard trapezoid utility blade sold everywhere. Buy blades in bulk; a sharp blade is safer because you push less.
It saves hunting for a spare on a ladder. The Klein 44306, REXBETI set and Milwaukee 48-22-1502 store blades in the handle.
Metal bodies like the WORKPRO, VOTREK and STANLEY 99 survive drops and look better longer. Plastic knives are fine for a junk drawer.

buyers_guide.q: Is a utility knife the same as a pocket knife?
buyers_guide.a: No. A utility knife takes cheap replaceable blades you swap when dull. A pocket knife has a fixed blade you sharpen. For boxes, carpet and drywall, a utility knife is easier to keep sharp.
